en: *Collection on the Perfect Cause for Rebirth through Secret Mantra*,
compiled by the monk Zhiguang, who received imperial edicts and was ordained at Yousheng Temple on Mount Shizifeng at Ganshui.

Compiled by the *shamon* Huizhen, Director of Ordination at the Great Qingliang Temple on Mount Wutai in the North; translated and finalized by the *shamon* Vajradhvaja, Chan Master Chongfa of Lushan. **The Ritual for Reciting Divine Mantras** Now, as for those who wish to recite and maintain *dhāraṇī* divine mantras: [The text continues with the ritual procedures.]
First, one must take refuge in the Three Jewels and generate the great bodhicitta;
only thereafter should one recite the mantra according to the ritual procedure.
Now, according to the ritual of the Five-Syllable Dhāraṇī,
there are four ways of reciting the divine mantra: the first is samādhi-recitation,
which means visualizing the mantra being recited.
Light radiates from the mouth of the *iṣṭadevatā* and enters one's own mouth,
circling to the right and settling within the moon disc at the heart,
like a crystal bead placed upon a clear mirror.
The mind should focus on this as being so.
Second is "mental recitation," which means visualizing the syllables of the mantra upon the moon-disk of the aforementioned mind.
The voice produced from the mouth is neither loud nor soft, neither slow nor hurried.
One should maintain mindfulness in this manner;
the resonance of the voice is like that of a ringing bell.
Third is vajra-recollection (*vajrasmṛti*).
This means that, based on the previous [stage], one enters the contemplation of syllables,
keeping the lips and teeth closely joined.
In the minor practice, one slightly moves the tongue while reciting this.
Fourth is the contemplation for subduing demons,
which means taking compassion as the internal foundation.
Externally manifesting an expression of majestic wrath,
one should recite this with knitted brows and a stern voice.
Although these four types differ from one another, [they share the same essence].
Not departing from a single thought constitutes non-duality.
Furthermore, there are two kinds:
first, the incalculable upholding of mindfulness.
That is to say: first, reciting without holding a mala and without fixed timing or number, maintaining the recitation constantly while walking, standing, sitting, or lying down;
second, reciting with a fixed number while holding a mala.
This means counting with the fingers using a rosary to determine a fixed number of times—
whether one hundred or one thousand— as appropriate for recitation.
If a person recites and maintains secret divine mantras in this manner:
One must receive and uphold [the teachings] by relying upon a teacher and the scriptures; furthermore,
one must seek out those who are proficient in the Sanskrit language so that they may provide definitive explanations of the words and phrases,
ensuring they are not corrupted or mispronounced.
Clearly discerning each part and maintaining single-minded devotion in recitation,
one should select any one of the four aforementioned methods of mindfulness and perform the recitation according to the ritual rules without interruption.
The supreme fruit you pray for will certainly be accomplished.

The Vidyārāja-mantra of the Great Vajracakra Vidyārāja: Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | Oṃ jvala jvala mahācakravartine cakrarāja saptasapta sarvate sarvate dharāṅgane svāhā | Svāhā | Dharaṇi svāhā | Jvalāṅgane | Samastacihnane | Dharani svāhā | Svāhā. The method for the recitation of Akṣobhya Tathāgata states: *The Vidyārāja-mantra of the Great Vajracakra Vidyārāja:* *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | Oṃ jvala jvala mahācakravartine cakrarāja saptasapta sarvate sarvate dharāṅgane svāhā | Svāhā | Dharaṇi svāhā | Jvalāṅgane | Samastacihnane | Dharani svāhā | Svāhā.* The ritual for the recitation of Akṣobhya Tathāgata says: [as above].
By reciting this mantra, one may [be purified from] re-entering a maṇḍala circle,
losing mindfulness, or breaking samādhi; as well as the two types of discipline— body and speech— of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas,
and the four pārājika offenses and the five ānantarya crimes.
All such karmic obstacles and transgressions shall be completely purified.
Furthermore, the *Amṛtakuṇḍalī-bodhisattva-japa-vidhi* states:
Next, one should form the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Vajracakra.
One who enters the maṇḍala by reciting the secret mantra receives the three types of bodhisattva vows that are unimpeded throughout the three times;
this occurs through the entry into the maṇḍala.
Throughout the body and mind, one is fully endowed with the samaya of non-action precepts, as numerous as the atoms within worlds as many as the atoms in ten *paramāṇu-koṭis* of lands.
This may occur through the bending and stretching, the bowing and looking up, the speaking of words and the exhaling of breath, or the arising of thoughts and the movement of mental activity.
For those who have forgotten the bodhicitta or regressed from their roots of virtue,
this supreme skillful means of mudrās and mantras— through recitation,
retention, and mental cultivation— is able to eliminate transgressions and faults.
The samaya, as before, becomes doubly radiant;
because it can purify body, speech, and mind,
one thereby accomplishes entry into all maṇḍalas.
Regarding the mudrā for obtaining the samaya of empowerment:
interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward,
and extend the two index fingers straight upward, keeping them side by side.
Wrap the two middle fingers around the first joints of the two index fingers so that their tips touch each other;
extend both thumbs straight and side by side.
Forming the mudrā at the heart, one should recite the secret mantra.
If one has not yet entered the maṇḍala and is not permitted to perform the ritual,
by means of this mantra, one may immediately enter the maṇḍala and perform the ritual.
This does not constitute the offense of stealing.
Regarding the *Jing fajie zhou* (Purification of the Dharma Realm Mantra): *Oṃ raṃ*. The *Yogācāra-padma-kula-japa-vidhi* states:
"If one touches an impure place, one should visualize [the syllable] upon the crown of the head."
There is a dharmadhātu-syllable that emits red light,
namely the syllable *ḷaṃ*.
One should empower all food with this syllable.
Thus, it does not constitute an impure touch.
This term should be added to all offerings, such as incense and flowers;
by emitting white light, there will be no impure touch.
All objects of offering pervade the entire Dharma-realm.
The Mantra for Mañjuśrī’s Protection of the Body: Oṃ cili chiling. The *Mañjuśrī-mūla-ekākṣara-dhāraṇī-sūtra* states:
If one recites this mantra, it can eliminate all calamities and obstacles,
all evil dreams, and all enemies; it can extinguish all karmic offenses,
including the five heinous crimes and the ten evil deeds.
It can eliminate all evil and heterodox incantations and can also accomplish all virtuous deeds;
among all various mantras, it is the heart-essence of all Buddhas.
It can cause all one's aspirations to be fully satisfied.
If one recites it once while generating the great resolve,
it will immediately protect one's own person.
If recited twice,
its power can protect one's companions;
if recited three times, [the same applies].
Its power can protect the people within a single household;
if recited four times,
its power can protect the people within an entire city.
If one recites it five times,
its power can protect all the people within a kingdom.
If one recites it six times, [the same applies].
Its power is able to protect the people of one world-system.
If recited seven times,
its power is able to protect the people of the four world-systems.

The One-Syllable Wheel-Turning King Dhāraṇī. The One-Syllable Wheel-Turning King Dhāraṇī: Oṃ bhu liṃ (pronounced *mù lóng yún* according to the direct phonetics). Regarding the "One-Syllable Heart-Dhāraṇī Sūtra" of the Final Dharma Age, it says:
The Buddha addressed the sons of the Buddhas: "You all should now listen well;
I shall now proclaim this dhāraṇī, which is fully endowed with all merits."
In the evil age of the future, when my Dharma is about to perish,
you shall be able during this time to protect and uphold my Final Dharma;
you shall be able to eliminate the evils of the world and the poisonous harm of all malevolent spirits.
As well as all gods, Māras, and humans—
should they hear the name of this dhāraṇī, all their various incantation methods will be spontaneously crushed and subdued.
After my parinirvāṇa, once the śarīras have been distributed, [this shall prevail].
One should conceal the various marks and signs and manifest a transformed body for this mantra.
The Buddha has two kinds of bodies: the true body (*dharmakāya*) and the transformation body (*nirmāṇakāya*).
If one can make offerings to either, the merit and virtue are no different.
This mantra is likewise so: all devas and humans who are able to give rise to a mind of rare wonder, and who receive, uphold, and make offerings to it,
shall obtain all manner of merits no different from my own person.
I have now briefly explained the merits of this King of Mantras;
it is the Three-Syllable Dhāraṇī. The Three-Syllable Dhāraṇī is: Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ. As stated in the *Yogamahātantrarāja-sūtra*:
The syllable Oṃ is the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana;
the syllable Āḥ is the Tathāgata Amitāyus;
the syllable Hūṃ is the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
Furthermore, the *Buddhabhāvanā-vidhi* states:
"By the power of the empowerment from reciting this syllable Oṃ,
even if one's visualization is not perfected, [one will attain success] within the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas."
The ocean-like clouds of all offerings, Through the mantras possessing accomplishment,
And by the truthfulness of all Buddhas, Which is established by the very nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*),
By the mere recitation of the syllable *A*, All karmic obstructions and hindrances are destroyed.
Attaining all that is pleasing and delightful,
equal to all Buddhas and surpassing all Māras, you shall be unable to be obstructed;
you should receive the vast offerings of all the world.
Through the empowerment of the syllable HŪṂ, tigers, wolves, various venomous insects,
and malicious humans and non-humans were all unable to overcome or subdue the Tathāgata when he first attained Buddhahood beneath the Bodhi tree.
By means of this mudrā and mantra, the hosts of celestial Māras are destroyed.
*The Great Cundī Dhāraṇī of the Heart of the Mother of the Seven Koṭis of Buddhas*. *NAMAḤ*.

The Buddha said: "This mantra can extinguish all karmic obstacles of the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes, and bring to fulfillment all pure dharmas and meritorious virtues.
Those who uphold this mantra..."
It makes no distinction between laypeople and monastics, nor does it concern whether one drinks alcohol, eats meat, or has a wife and children;
nor does it select between the pure and the impure.
Relying solely upon my Dharma, there is nothing that cannot be accomplished.
If one recites this with a sincere heart,
it can extend the lifespan of sentient beings with short lives and eliminate immeasurable suffering from illness.
Even the disease of kāmalā can be cured;
how much more so other ailments? It is impossible that they would not be eliminated and healed.
If one recites this mantra one hundred and eight times, [the result will follow].
In this manner, they continued without interruption for forty-nine days.
Whenever there were auspicious or calamitous events, whether good or evil,
the Bodhisattva Cundā caused the two holy beings to constantly follow that person.
All thoughts of good and evil arising in the mind shall be reported to them one by one at their very ears.
Furthermore, recite this mantra.
It causes kings, ministers, elders, brahmins,
and others to give rise to feelings of love and respect; upon seeing it, they immediately rejoice,
and whatever their wishes may be, all are fully accomplished.
If there are those who lack merit and auspicious marks,
who seek office but do not advance, and are oppressed by poverty and suffering,
they should constantly recite this mantra.
It enables one to obtain the merit of a Wheel-Turning King in the present life;
whatever rank or position one seeks shall surely be fulfilled.
If one constantly maintains this recitation, water cannot drown them and fire cannot burn them.
Poisons, weapons, enemies, and the suffering of illness shall all be unable to harm them.
Furthermore, if one recites it according to the ritual method for one million times,
one will immediately attain rebirth in the pure lands of the ten directions.
Having served various Buddhas and heard the wondrous Dharma, one shall swiftly realize Bodhi.

The Great Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Sitātapatrā Hṛdaya Dhāraṇī: Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ sarvathā rakṣa māṃ sadā svāhā | Oṃ āḥ hūṃ jvala jvalana mārakleśajinamardane mardane jinamardane jinamārakleśapradame phaṭ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā || The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* states: [as follows].
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"This mantra of the Buddha’s Uṣṇīṣa gives birth to all Buddhas throughout the ten directions."
By means of this mantra-heart, the Tathāgatas of the ten directions have attained unsurpassed, right, and universal enlightenment;
the Tathāgatas of the ten directions uphold this mantra-heart.
Subduing all māras and restraining all non-Buddhists,
the Tathāgatas of the ten directions ride upon this mantra-heart;
seated upon precious lotus flowers in lands as numerous as motes of dust, they turn the Great Wheel of Dharma.
He strokes their heads and bestows upon them the prediction of enlightenment, delivering them from all sufferings—
namely, those of the hells, hungry ghosts, and animals, as well as blindness, deafness, and muteness.
They are simultaneously liberated from the five types of suffering and all calamities.
Calamities from bandits, calamities from armies, calamities from kings,
and calamities from prisons, as well as hunger, thirst, and poverty, shall be dissolved and dispersed through mere recollection.
If I were to describe the merits of this mantra, [it would be endless].
From dawn until dusk, the sounds continue in succession;
even within the intervals between words and phrases, there is no overlap.
Even throughout kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, one could never reach their end.
If sentient beings write down this mantra on paper, silk,
or white cotton cloth and store it in a fragrant pouch,
even though their minds are dull and they are unable to recite or memorize it;
Whether worn upon the body or inscribed within the home,
it should be known that for as long as such a person lives,
they shall not be harmed by any poison whatsoever.
Ānanda, if there are sentient beings in the final age after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa who can recite this themselves or teach others to recite it,
they cannot be drowned by water nor burned by fire.
If great or small poisonous vapors enter this person's mouth, they will turn into the taste of nectar (*amṛta*).
No malevolent stars, ghosts, spirits, or poisoners shall be able to cause harm.
One should know that this is a mantra.
There are always eighty-four thousand nayutas of Ganges-sand kotis of the families of Vajragarbha-rāja Bodhisattvas,
each accompanied by their respective hosts of vajra-beings.
They shall become his retinue, attending upon him day and night.
Even if there are sentient beings who, with a distracted mind and not in a state of samādhi,
merely recollect this in their minds or maintain it through speech.
These Vajra Kings constantly follow those sons of good family;
how much more so those who possess the resolute bodhicitta?
These Vajragarbha Kings—
With focused effort, they secretly and swiftly awaken that divine consciousness;
at that moment, this person is able to remember eighty-four thousand *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* eons.
Having attained thorough and pervasive knowledge, they are free from doubt.
From kalpa to kalpa, they will never be born into states of poverty, lowliness, or unpleasantness.
Even if these sentient beings themselves do not perform meritorious deeds, [they shall still attain this].
All the merits of all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions are bestowed upon this person.
By virtue of this, they shall attain [these merits] for as many asaṃkhyeya kalpas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, even unto unspeakably unspeakable numbers of kalpas.
They are always born in the same place as all Buddhas.
Their immeasurable merits are like a cluster of akṣa fruits;
cultivated together in the same place, they never become dispersed.
Therefore, it can cause those who have broken the precepts to purify their roots of virtue;
it enables those who have not yet attained the precepts to attain them;
and it causes those who have not yet practiced with diligence to achieve such diligence.
Those without wisdom shall attain wisdom;
those who are not pure shall swiftly attain purity;
and those who do not observe the precepts of fasting shall spontaneously fulfill them.
When this good man maintains this mantra,
even if he has transgressed the prohibitive precepts prior to receiving them,
all the offenses of breaking the precepts committed after maintaining the mantra [shall be purified].
All karmic offenses, whether grave or light, are simultaneously extinguished.
Even if one has consumed alcohol or eaten the five pungent roots and various kinds of impurities,
all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, devas, rishis, ghosts, and spirits [will accept it].
It shall not be considered a transgression.
Even if one does not construct an altar, enter a dharma-hall, or practice the Way,
if one recites and upholds this mantra, [the merit will be attained].
It is equivalent to the merit of entering the dharma-arena to practice the Way.
Even if one has committed the five heinous crimes of immediate retribution,
or the four parājikas and eight saṃghāvaśeṣas of bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, [this merit shall absolve them].
Having recited this mantra,
such heavy karma will be completely eliminated without leaving so much as a hair’s breadth, just as a fierce wind scatters a heap of sand.
If there are sentient beings who, since immeasurable kalpas past,
have accumulated all manner of light and heavy karmic obstacles for which they have not yet repented from previous lives;
If one can read, recite, or transcribe this mantra,
wearing it upon the body or placing it in one's dwelling, house, garden, or villa,
then such accumulated karma will be dissolved like snow melting in boiling water.
Before long, they all attained the realization of the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
If there are women who have not yet borne sons or daughters and wish to conceive, [they should do so].
If one mindfully recollects this with sincerity, or wears it upon the body,
one will give birth to sons or daughters endowed with merit and wisdom.
Those who seek long life shall immediately obtain long life.
After the end of life, one will be reborn in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions according to one's vows.
If there are famines, epidemics, or calamities of war and bandits in various lands,
one should transcribe this divine mantra and place it upon the four gates of the city or atop a caitya banner.
It shall cause the people of the land to welcome, prostrate to, revere, and make offerings to [the image],
whereby all calamities and misfortunes will be entirely extinguished;
winds and rains will follow their proper seasons, and the five grains will be abundant and prosperous.
The myriad subjects shall enjoy peace and happiness, and no calamities or obstacles shall arise.
Should malevolent stars appear or various portents of disaster manifest,
they shall all be utterly extinguished within this land protected by the mantra.
An area of twelve yojanas shall be established as a consecrated boundary (sīmā),
into which no evil portents or calamities can ever enter.
For this reason, the Tathāgata proclaims this mantra.
You and all future practitioners should not give rise to doubt or regret regarding this mantra-heart.
O son of good family!
If one cannot attain mental penetration within this body born of one's parents,
then the Tathāgatas of the ten directions would be speaking falsehoods.

The Root Mantra of the Great Jewel Pavilion (Mahāratnakūṭa-mūla-mantra): Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | Oṃ vikurvaṇe prabhāse tathāgate | Tathāgatatejodhṛte | Mame mame | Subhare | Vikrama-sāre | Āveśaya | Hūṃ hūṃ | Cchinda cchinda mohe vaṅkike | Vajra-niṣṭhite | Svāhā. The *Susthitadhāraṇī Sūtra* states:
If there are sentient beings who hear this dhāraṇī,
receive and uphold it, read and recite it, cultivate and remember it,
or even merely hear its name, seeking great accomplishment.
Or again, one may touch it with the hand or wear it upon the body;
or merely gaze upon it with the eyes, or write it in a scripture,
or inscribe it on silk or paper, or write it upon a wall.
If any sentient beings should behold [this],
even those who have committed the five heinous crimes or the four grave offenses, those who slander the True Dharma or the noble ones,
or those who hunt, slaughter, or act as butchers— [all shall be purified].
Those who are blind, deaf, hunchbacked, mute, or afflicted with leprosy;
those who are impoverished, lowly, or oppressed by the snares of Māra,
wrong views, or malevolent stars— all such persons, as well as all classes of sentient beings throughout the four modes of birth.
Those who hear the name of this dhāraṇī will certainly realize unsurpassed bodhi;
whether it is written upon clothing, placed atop a banner, or on a wooden plaque,
or even by merely hearing its sound or touching it with the hand.
Furthermore, when their shadow touches others,
those individuals will certainly never retreat from unsurpassed bodhi;
they shall be able to attain manifold merits in this present life and remain far removed from all transgressions.
They shall be revered and loved by all in the world;
they shall receive offerings everywhere,
including from all kings, princes, ministers, and those in the royal harems.
Together with their retinues, they all attained joy;
they were freed from poverty and did not undergo worldly suffering,
nor the calamities of poison, weapons, water, fire, and so forth.
Various wild beasts and the like cannot cause them harm;
they are free from all terrors and entirely devoid of disease.
At the time of death, their minds remain undisturbed.
All Buddhas appear before them to offer consolation;
they sleep in peace and awaken in peace, even seeing hundreds of thousands of Buddha-fields and being surrounded by Buddhas and Bodhisattvas within their dreams.
All Māras shall be unable to create obstacles;
all enemies shall find no opportunity;
and one’s roots of goodness shall increase and be attained.
The merit is immeasurable;
how much more so for those who can maintain the recitation over a long period—their merit cannot be calculated.
Furthermore, it does not depend on specific days or times, nor is it limited by fasting or ritual observances.
If one constantly recites this one hundred and eight times at the clear dawn, all that is sought shall be accomplished.

This is the Heart Mantra of the Great Jewel Pavilion. The Heart Mantra of the Great Jewel Pavilion: Oṃ māṇibhadre hūṃ. If this heart mantra is recited one hundred thousand times, [all goals will be attained].
One will immediately see all the Tathāgatas.
By reciting it two hundred thousand times,
one will attain the vision of all Buddha-fields.
If one recites it three hundred thousand times,
one will succeed in all maṇḍalas,
and all mantra-dharmas will be fully accomplished.
If one recites it even as many as one million times,
one will attain the Buddha-ground of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas and enter into the same assembly as all Tathāgatas.
If one has committed the five heinous crimes, slandered the noble ones, or slandered the true Dharma—
such that one ought to enter the Avīci Hell—
one should recite this mantra one thousand times.
All committed karmic offenses will be completely extinguished;
one shall attain the stage of non-retrogression, realize the wisdom of recollecting past lives, and achieve purity of the six sense faculties.
Furthermore, one shall obtain various worldly undertakings, which will be accomplished according to one's wishes.
The Great Jewel Pavilion Heart Mantra. The Great Jewel Pavilion Heart Mantra: Oṃ maṇidhāri hūṃ phaṭ. If one recites this Heart Mantra ten thousand times, it will be fulfilled.
All gods and spirits who create obstacles shall come to prostrate at his feet and say:
"O Vidyādhara, protect us; do not take our lives."
Whatever I have commanded shall certainly be understood and fully accomplished by all.
By reciting this one hundred thousand times,
one shall behold all the Tathāgatas.
Those Tathāgatas spoke these words:
"Noble son, regarding all the Buddha-fields where you wish to go,
you shall attain them according to your will without any obstruction."
Furthermore, one shall attain various mundane and supramundane dharmas;
whatever the mind desires and seeks shall all be accomplished.
The *Guṇakūṭa Dhāraṇī*: Namaḥ mañjaye | Namaḥ mañjuśriye | Namaḥ samantāya | Sinin hurulu | Sinirulu | Kilpa kilpa | Sinaye | Pruye svāhā. The *Mahāsannipāta Sūtra* states:
If a person recites this mantra once,
it is as if they have performed forty-five thousand four hundred prostrations before the *Sūtra of the Names of the Great Buddhas*,
and likewise as if they have turned the *Great Canon* six hundred and fifty-four thousand times.
Having committed transgressions exceeding ten buddha-fields,
they enter the Avīci Great Hell;
there they undergo retribution for kalpas until it is exhausted, at which point they are reborn again.
If one recites this mantra once,
all their transgressions will be completely extinguished and they shall not enter hell;
at the end of life, they will certainly be reborn in the Western World.

One shall attain the highest grade of rebirth in the presence of Amitābha Buddha. If there are good sons or good daughters who,
with utmost sincerity, pay respectful homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acala, and uphold this dhāraṇī,
the five sins of immediate retribution previously committed by them [shall be extinguished].
All the transgressions of the four grave offenses, the ten evil deeds, the disparagement of the worthy and holy ones,
and the slandering of the true Dharma shall be entirely extinguished.
At the time of death, that Buddha Aśoka—
Together with various bodhisattvas, they appeared before him,
praising and consoling him to bring him joy,
and further addressed him, saying: "We have now come to welcome you."
"You should follow me to the buddha-field from which I have come.
After you pass away there,
you will certainly be reborn in the pure buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya."

The Root Mantra of Śākyamuni, King Who Extirpates Evil Destinies. *Śākyamuni-māraṇa-pāpa-gati-rāja-mūla-mantra:* Oṃ namo mārakṛtante | sarvamartyante parikhaṇḍi nīranye | tathāgate | arhante | samyak-sambuddhaye tadyathā | oṃ khaṇḍi khaṇḍi | sarvabhāṣye | vikhaṇḍi | jahi vikhaṇḍi | sarvakarma | āvaraṇe | vikhaṇḍi kuru | Svāhā. The *Dharani Sutra for Deliverance from Suffering and Calamity* states: [The mantra continues as follows: Oṃ namo mārakṛtante | sarvamartyante parikhaṇḍi nīranye | tathāgate | arhante | samyak-sambuddhaye | tadyathā | oṃ khaṇḍi khaṇḍi | sarvabhāṣye | vikhaṇḍi | jahi vikhaṇḍi | sarvakarma | āvaraṇe | vikhaṇḍi kuru | Svāhā. The *Dharani Sutra for Deliverance from Suffering and Calamity* says: [End of excerpt].
If there are good men or good women who,
with utmost sincerity, pay homage to the Tathāgata King Who Extinguishes Evil Destinies and uphold this mantra,
they shall constantly remember their past lives for fourteen thousand kalpas.
In whatever place they are born, they shall obtain a male body,
be endowed with all faculties, have deep faith in cause and effect,
be skilled in various arts and crafts, and possess a profound understanding of all treatises.
Delighting in the practice of giving, he renounces all desires;
refraining from unwholesome deeds, he is free from all peril and fear;
endowed with right mindfulness and wisdom, he is beloved and respected by all.
Constantly associating with virtuous friends and perpetually hearing the true Dharma,
they never for a moment abandon the aspiration for enlightenment,
adorning themselves with all manner of meritorious virtues.
Possessing excellent ethical discipline, they fear all evil deeds;
they are never lacking in anything, being gentle, pliant, and delighting in tranquility;
they constantly experience happiness among gods and humans.
May they swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment,
never regressing from the ten pāramitās,
and may they always bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
All their practices are not for the sake of self-benefit alone;
wherever they are born, they always behold the Buddhas,
uphold the true Dharma, and join the assembly of noble sages.

The Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Vimalaprabhā Dhāraṇī. The Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Vimalaprabhā Dhāraṇī: Oṃ ḍiḥ jvalita-sarva-tathāgata-jvālā-krodha-mānaka-dṛṣṭi-saṃhara āyuḥ-saṃskāra-jīvitaṃ svāhā. The *Buddhoṣṇīṣavimalaprabhā-sarvatathāgata-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra* states: Oṃ ḍiḥ jvalita-sarva-tathāgata-jvālā-krodha-mānaka-dṛṣṭi-saṃhara āyuḥ-saṃskāra-jīvitaṃ svāhā. Oṃ jvalita-sarva-tathāgata-samanta-śrī-teja-māla-vijaya-mati-śuddhe svāhā. The *Buddhoṣṇīṣavimalaprabhā-sarvatathāgata-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra* says: [as above].
This dhāraṇī was proclaimed by ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
If there are sentient beings who see, hear, or rejoice in it, [they shall attain great merit].
All sinful karmas of the three periods of time,
which would otherwise lead to rebirth in the hells, the evil destinies, or even as animals,
shall all be utterly destroyed.
If this mantra is written and placed within a stūpa,
it is equivalent to the entire bodily relics of as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in nine hundred thousand koṭis of nayutas of Gaṅgā rivers—
each and every one of those Tathāgatas.
It is placed within the stūpa without any difference.
If there are those who conceive reverence for this stūpa,
all their past karma of short life will be eliminated.
Furthermore, their lifespan will be increased and they will be protected by the various devas.
When this person’s life ends and they cast off this body,
they shall immediately attain rebirth in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
If one recites it even once,
it is as if one has planted roots of goodness in the presence of as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in ten Gaṅgā rivers,
thereby obtaining great merit and retribution.
The five deeds of immediate retribution shall all be completely extinguished;
even those in the realms of hell, the animal kingdom,
and the world of Yama shall all attain liberation from every karmic obstruction and sin.
Furthermore, one shall obtain long life;
when one's life ends, one will be reborn in the World of Peace and Bliss.
This applies even to those who recite with single-minded concentration.
Those who have long suffered from sores and wounds shall find them healed;
whatever they seek in their hearts, they shall all obtain.
Furthermore, if there are others who hear the sound of this recitation, [the same shall occur].
All karmic obstructions shall be completely liberated.
Even the sound of their recitation, reaching the ears of animals, insects, ants, and all such beings, shall cause them to be entirely liberated from their karmic paths.
If one digs up skeletal remains in a cemetery,
recites a mantra over the sand and soil twenty-one times, and scatters it upon the bones,
that person’s consciousness will follow to whatever direction or location those remains have gone.
Those who have fallen into hell will all be completely liberated and reborn in the Heaven of the Sugatas.
If one recites this one hundred thousand times, [the same result shall be attained].
At the time of death,
they will be bound by the neck with a rope by the messengers of King Yama and dragged into the realm of Yama;
within that realm are all the various hells.
All [obstacles] are utterly destroyed, giving rise instead to fear;
they are immediately made to turn back, whereby one attains liberation.
This refers to the practitioner, who is a messenger of the Dharma King.
Abiding in the path of meditative concentration (dhyāna), one is free from doubt;
desiring to be born in the world of peace and bliss, one will be reborn there in accordance with one's vow.
The Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-vijaya-dhāraṇī and the Vijaya-dhāraṇī are as set forth in the original sūtra.
The Uṣṇīṣavijayā-hṛdaya-mantra. The *Uṣṇīṣavijayā-dhāraṇī-sūtra* states: "This mantra can destroy all hells. Oṃ vimalatejo-jvalita-vijaya-tejo-hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
The *Uṣṇīṣavijayā-dhāraṇī-sūtra* states: "This mantra can destroy all hells."
From the realm of King Yama and the sufferings of the animal rebirth,
they shall turn toward the auspicious paths;
this mantra is inconceivable and possesses great supernormal power.
If there should be anyone who hears [this name] even once,
all evil karma created in previous lives will be completely extinguished,
and they shall obtain a pure, supreme, and wondrous body.
One will remember and never forget the various celestial realms where one is born within the Buddha-fields wherever one may be reborn.
If a person wishes to briefly recollect this mantra, their lifespan shall be restored and increased.
Their body, speech, and mind will be pure and free from suffering;
according to their merit and benefit, they shall all receive peace and security,
and they shall be gazed upon by all Tathāgatas.
All celestial deities shall constantly serve as his guardians;
he will be revered by all people, and all evil obstacles will be eliminated.
All Bodhisattvas shall likewise provide him with protection.
They enter at will, without any obstruction, into the pure lands of all Buddhas, the celestial palaces of all devas, and the profound practices and vows of all bodhisattvas.
After casting off this body, one will immediately attain rebirth in various subtle and wondrous Buddha-fields.
The Six-Syllable Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva: Oṃ Maṇipadme Hūṃ. As stated in the *Sūtra of the Adorned Jewel King*:
These six syllables of the Great Vidya-mantra are the subtle,
essential heart-mind of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
If a person upholds and recites this mantra, [they shall attain liberation].
During the time of recitation, there will be an assembly of Tathāgatas numbering as many as ninety Ganges Rivers,
along with Bodhisattvas as numerous as motes of dust,
and devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and space-dwelling deities who will come to provide protection.
Seven generations of their lineage shall all attain liberation.
The various insects within their bellies shall attain the rank of non-retrogressive bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, if one recites according to the ritual method, [the same result shall be achieved].
Such a person shall attain inexhaustible eloquence,
a mass of pure wisdom, and great compassion;
day by day, they shall fully realize the perfected merit of the six pāramitās.
The breath exhaled from this person's mouth,
upon touching the bodies of others who are touched by it,
immediately gives rise to a mind of loving-kindness and causes them to abandon all poisonous hatred.
One shall become an irreversible Bodhisattva and swiftly realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
If anyone wears and maintains this mantra, [they shall attain these benefits].
Then, being identical to the Tathāgata’s vajra-body,
if one touches the body of another person with one's hand,
both those who receive that touch and all sentient beings who see it [will likewise be transformed].
They shall all swiftly attain the rank of bodhisattva and forever be exempt from the sufferings of birth,
old age, sickness, death, and separation from loved ones.
Furthermore, it is as if there were men, women, and others filling the four great continents.
All shall attain the rank of a Bodhisattva of the seventh stage.
The merits possessed by that assembly of Bodhisattvas are no different from the merit of reciting this mantra once.
If a person transcribes this six-syllable mahāvidyā dhāraṇī,
it is no different from transcribing the eighty-four thousand treasuries of the Dharma.
If one fashions [an image] out of celestial gold and jewels...
The merit of writing even a single character from among these six syllables is not equaled by as many images of the Tathāgatas as there are atoms in a speck of dust.
If anyone should obtain this six-syllable vidyā-mantra...
The poisons of greed, hatred, and delusion cannot defile such a person.
Furthermore, anyone who wears or carries this within their body will likewise not be defiled by the maladies of greed, hatred, and delusion.
Regarding the Five-Syllable Heart Mantra of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra* states that the five-syllable mantra possesses supreme characteristics: *A RA PA TSA NA*.
If a person recites it even once,
it is as if they have recited the eighty-four thousand twelve Vedas;
if they recite it twice, [the merit is doubled].
Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra follow and bestow their grace upon them;
the Dharma-protecting benevolent deities stand before such persons.
Furthermore, O son of good family or daughter of good family:
If there is one who can maintain this mantra and recite it even once,
they will immediately enter into the equality of all dharmas of the Tathāgata;
all letters, as well, are equal.
One will swiftly attain the accomplishment of Mahāprajñā.
Furthermore, reciting it even once can eliminate all hardships and calamities for the practitioner.
If one recites it twice,
the grave sins of birth and death accumulated over billions of kalpas will be extinguished;
if one recites it three times, samādhi will manifest before one.
If one recites it four times, one will not forget the dhāraṇī;
if one recites it five times, one will swiftly attain unsurpassed bodhi.
If a person dwells alone in a quiet and secluded place with a single-minded focus, [they shall achieve this].
Having constructed a five-syllable wheel maṇḍala according to the Brahma-script and recited the mantra for one full month in accordance with the ritual rules,
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva will immediately manifest his form.
Or they may expound the essential points of the Dharma in mid-air;
at that time, the practitioner attains the knowledge of past lives,
unimpeded eloquence, and mastery over the supernormal powers.
With supreme vows accomplished and merit and wisdom fully perfected,
one will swiftly realize the Dharmakāya of the Tathāgata;
it suffices merely to believe and accept this with the mind.
Having received the transmission of the *Cakṣuṣmatī-vidyā* (Wheel-Syllable Contemplation) from the Master after sixteen lifetimes, he attained the certainty of perfect enlightenment.

This is the Amṛta-mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva: *Namo Ratnatrayāya | Namah Āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛtavati svāhā.* The *Avalokiteśvara-dhāraṇī-sūtra* states:
If one wishes to recite this mantra,
all past and present offenses— including the four grave pārājika transgressions, the five heinous crimes (ānantarya),
the slandering of the Vaipulya sūtras, and the sins of an icchantika— [shall be extinguished].
All [obstacles] are completely extinguished without remainder;
body and mind become light and agile, and wisdom becomes clear and penetrating.
Whether by means of body or speech, one is able to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings.
If there are sentient beings who have extensively committed all manner of crimes, including those of immediate retribution,
should they encounter the shadow of this mantra-holding person briefly falling upon their bodies,
or suddenly engage in conversation with them, or hear the sound of their voice.
That person’s karmic obstacles will all be completely extinguished.
Furthermore, if one wishes to benefit all sentient beings,
whenever it rains, one should [perform this practice].
Arousing great compassion, he looks up toward the sky and recites the mantra twenty-one times;
all sentient beings touched by those drops of rain [are benefited].
All evil karma and heavy transgressions will be completely extinguished, and one shall obtain all benefit and happiness.

The Mantra of the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light Buddha: Nama amogha-dhṛte | dhṛti-ru | dhṛti-ye | pramara-tejā | tathāgate | araha-dhite | samyak-sambuddhe-tatte | oṃ dhṛte dhṛte | mahā-dhṛte dhṛte-rasate | svāhā. The *Sūtra on the Merits of the Seven Medicine-Buddhas* states:
When the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha attained bodhi, by the power of his original vow,
he beheld all sentient beings encountering the suffering of various diseases.
Diseases such as emaciation, malarial fever, wasting, and jaundice;
or being afflicted by malevolent spells and sorcery;
or having a short lifespan, or dying an untimely death.
Desiring to cause the suffering of these illnesses to be eliminated and their aspirations to be fulfilled,
he recited this dhāraṇī from within the light.
If one sees any man or woman afflicted by the suffering of illness, [one should recite it for them].
One should single-mindedly provide for that patient with pure water for rinsing the mouth;

There are four types of distinctions regarding rosaries: the superior, the most excellent, the middling, and the inferior.
One thousand and eight beads constitute the superior; one hundred and eight beads are the most excellent;
fifty-four beads are the middling; and twenty-seven beads are the inferior class.
Holding two rosaries at the heart, with a mind of meditative concentration free from discursive thought,
focused one-pointedly on the yoga of the deity, one will achieve accomplishment through both the methods of principle and phenomena.
Whether placed upon a topknot, worn around the body, or positioned on the neck or the arms.
The discourse that has been taught constitutes the recitation; by this recitation, one purifies the three karmas.
By placing it upon the crown of the head, one purifies the immediate transgressions (*ānantarya*); by wearing it around the neck, one purifies the four grave offenses (*caturmahāpatti*);
by holding it on the arm, one eliminates all sins, enabling the practitioner to quickly attain purification.
If one cultivates true mantras and dhāraṇīs, and recollects the names of the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas, one shall obtain immeasurable and supreme merit;
all sought-after sublime vows shall be fulfilled.
This concludes the *Collection for Rebirth through the Perfection of Secret Mantra*.
